source.text: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹתהַבֹּטְחִ֥ים בַּיהוָ֑ה כְּֽהַר־צִיּ֥וֹן לֹא־יִ֝מּ֗וֹט לְעוֹלָ֥ם יֵשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents. Those who trust in YHWH [are] like Mount Zion, not it will be shaken, forever it will remain.

en.L: A song of ascents. Those who trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are] like Mount Zion, [which] will not be shaken; it remains forever.
en.B: A song of ascents. Whoever trusts in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is like Mount Zion: nothing can shake it; it stays in place forever.
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. People who trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are like Mount Zion. Nothing can shake that mountain. It will stand forever.

fr.L: Cantique des montées. Ceux qui se confient {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|en Yahvé}} [sont] comme le mont Sion, [qui] ne chancelle pas ; il demeure pour toujours.
fr.B: Cantique des montées. Celui qui se confie {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|en Yahvé}} est comme le mont Sion : rien ne peut l’ébranler ; il reste en place pour toujours.
fr.R: Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem. Les gens qui ont confiance dans {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sont comme le mont Sion. Rien ne peut faire bouger cette montagne. Elle tiendra pour toujours.

decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Mount Zion: the hill of the temple
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill in Jerusalem where the temple stood, the place God chose to live among his people (2:6; 132:13-14).
The verb (yashav) means to sit, stay or dwell. Here it means the mountain stays where it is; some take it as "is inhabited forever".

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem

source.text: יְֽרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הָרִים֮ סָבִ֪יב לָ֥הּ וַ֭יהוָה סָבִ֣יב לְעַמּ֑וֹ מֵ֝עַתָּ֗ה וְעַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Jerusalem — mountains [are] around it, and YHWH [is] around his people from now and until forever.

en.L: Jerusalem — mountains [are] around her, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people from now and until forever.
en.B: Mountains ring Jerusalem all around, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is all around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, from now on and forever.
en.R: The hills stand all around Jerusalem. In the same way, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is all around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people to protect them, now and forever.

fr.L: Jérusalem — des montagnes [sont] autour d’elle, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] autour de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, dès maintenant et jusqu’à toujours.
fr.B: Des montagnes entourent Jérusalem, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} entoure {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, dès maintenant et pour toujours.
fr.R: Les collines se dressent tout autour de Jérusalem. De la même façon, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est tout autour de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple pour le protéger, maintenant et pour toujours.

decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands on hills with higher hills around it, such as the Mount of Olives to the east. The hills were a natural defense, and the LORD is a better one.
In the Hebrew a city is feminine, "her"; Balanced and Readable name the city, Literal keeps "her".
Readable says what the picture of surrounding means.

source.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֪א יָנ֡וּחַ שֵׁ֤בֶט הָרֶ֗שַׁע עַל֮ גּוֹרַ֪ל הַֽצַּדִּ֫יקִ֥ים לְמַ֡עַן לֹא־יִשְׁלְח֖וּ הַצַּדִּיקִ֨ים בְּעַוְלָ֬תָה יְדֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For not will rest [the] scepter of wickedness on [the] lot of the righteous, so that not will stretch out the righteous in injustice their hands.

en.L: For the scepter of wickedness will not rest on the lot of the righteous, so that the righteous will not stretch out their hands to injustice.
en.B: Wicked rule will not stay in place over the land that belongs to the righteous, or even the righteous might reach out their hands to do wrong.
en.R: Wicked rulers will not always control the land of people who do what is right. If they did, even good people might start doing wrong.

fr.L: Car le sceptre de la méchanceté ne reposera pas sur le lot des justes, afin que les justes n’étendent pas leurs mains vers l’injustice.
fr.B: Le pouvoir des méchants ne restera pas sur la terre qui revient aux justes, sinon les justes eux-mêmes pourraient tendre la main pour faire le mal.
fr.R: Les chefs méchants ne domineront pas toujours le pays des gens qui font ce qui est bien. Sinon, même les gens bons pourraient se mettre à faire le mal.

decisions.choice: the scepter of wickedness: wicked rule
decisions.reason: A scepter (shevet) is the rod of a ruler. The picture is of wicked people, perhaps foreign rulers, governing God's people.

decisions.choice: the lot: the land given by lot
decisions.reason: Israel's land was divided among the tribes and families by lot (Joshua 14:2; 18:10), so "lot" means the land a family received as its share.

decisions.choice: so that ... not: to keep the righteous from wrong
decisions.reason: The LORD will not let wicked rule last, so that the righteous are not pushed into doing wrong themselves under its pressure.

decisions.choice: the righteous (B); people who do what is right, good people (R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, Readable says "people who do what is right" for the righteous.

decisions.choice: "les justes" for tsaddiqim at Literal and Balanced; Readable describes them
decisions.reason: The terms note sets "le juste" for tsaddiq. Readable says "people who do what is right" and "good people", as the English Readable does.

records.literal_gloss: Do good, YHWH, to the good, and to [the] upright in their hearts.

en.L: Do good, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to the good, and to [those who are] upright in their hearts.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be good to good people, to all whose hearts are upright.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be good to people who are good and who want to do what is right.

fr.L: Fais du bien, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, aux bons, et à [ceux qui sont] droits dans leur cœur.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sois bon pour ceux qui sont bons, pour tous ceux qui ont le cœur droit.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sois bon pour les gens qui sont bons et qui veulent faire ce qui est juste.

decisions.choice: upright in their hearts: honest within
decisions.reason: The upright (yesharim) are straight, not crooked; "in their hearts" means in their thoughts and intentions. Verse 5 sets them against those who turn to crooked ways.

decisions.choice: who want to do what is right
decisions.reason: Readable says what an upright heart is (m1).

source.text: וְהַמַּטִּ֤ים עַֽקַלְקַלּוֹתָ֗ם יוֹלִיכֵ֣ם יְ֭הוָה אֶת־פֹּעֲלֵ֣י הָאָ֑וֶן שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [those who] turn aside [to] their crooked [ways], YHWH will lead them away with [the] doers of wickedness. Peace [be] on Israel.

en.L: But [as for] those who turn aside [to] their crooked [ways], {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will lead them away with the doers of wickedness. Peace [be] upon Israel.
en.B: But as for people who wander off onto crooked paths, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will drive them away with all who do evil. May Israel have peace!
en.R: But some people leave the right road and follow crooked paths. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will send them away with everyone who does evil. May Israel have peace!

fr.L: Mais [quant à] ceux qui se détournent [vers] leurs [chemins] tortueux, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les emmènera avec ceux qui font le mal. Paix sur Israël !
fr.B: Mais ceux qui s’égarent sur des chemins tortueux, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les chassera avec tous ceux qui font le mal. Qu’Israël ait la paix !
fr.R: Mais certaines personnes quittent le bon chemin et suivent des chemins tordus. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les renverra avec tous ceux qui font le mal. Qu’Israël ait la paix !

decisions.reason: The word ('aqalqallot) means winding or twisted; it is used of crooked paths (Judges 5:6). It is the opposite of the upright of verse 4.

decisions.choice: lead them away: drive out, as captives
decisions.reason: The verb (halak, causative) means to lead away; the same word is used of being led off into exile or to judgment.

decisions.choice: peace on Israel: a closing blessing
decisions.reason: The psalm ends with a blessing on the whole people, as 128:6 does.

decisions.choice: leave the right road and follow crooked paths
alternatives: turn aside to their crooked ways
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture of turning off a straight road (m1).
